basics.name: Changyue (William) Zhao
basics.label: Master of Biostatistics Student
basics.summary: Master of Biostatistics student at Duke University developing foundation-model and LLM-agent approaches to biomedical analysis, and deep learning methods for biomedical data analysis and multimodal integration.

highlights: Selected coursework: Statistical Methods for Learning and Discovery; Deep Learning for Health Data; High-Dimensional Statistics and Machine Learning; Real Analysis; Statistical Inference (Ph.D. Level).

education.studyType: Bachelor of Science; Minor in Computer Science
highlights: Selected coursework: Mathematical Analysis; Theory of Statistics; Regression and Correlated Data; Statistical Machine Learning; Applied Multivariate Methods; Algorithms and Data Structures; Graduate Data Mining.
Graduated with High Distinction and received the Buehler Memorial Undergraduate Award as one of eight nominees.
CLA Dean’s List, Fall 2023 to Spring 2025.

education.institution: Shandong University of Finance and Economics
highlights: Selected coursework: Advanced Mathematics; Linear Algebra; Probability Theory and Statistics; Applied Statistics; Python; Microeconomics; Finance.
SDUFE First-Prize Scholarship in 2022 and 2023.

projects.name: L-STAR
projects.description: I developed a workflow that uses visual LLM comparisons to select spatial domain detection methods and combine their clusterings into a consensus tissue partition.
highlights: Built structured prompts, repeated comparisons of spatial maps and optional histology, JSON logs, and win-rate-based method selection.
Implemented consensus clustering with co-assignment matrices and average linkage, plus an all-wise comparison mode that aggregates repeated rankings with one LLM call per repeat.

Designed experiments across six spatial transcriptomics datasets to separate the effects of method selection and clustering aggregation, including ensemble-size, alternative-LLM, and fixed-method baselines.

Built marker-gene-based annotation with spot- and cell-level labels and an Unknown option; evaluated agreement with manual annotations using BioLORD-2023 embeddings and within-dataset permutation tests.
Audited sensitivity to color palettes, presentation order, and redundant candidates through ranking agreement, selected-method overlap, and clustering stability.

projects.name: LLM-Guided Pseudotime Analysis
projects.description: I developed pseudotime-agent, an end-to-end Python package that coordinates R/Seurat analysis and LLM inference through LangGraph, from evidence generation to per-cell pseudotime estimation.
highlights: Designed parallel UMAP and t-SNE annotation branches, concurrent lineage-family adjudication, and cross-embedding trajectory fusion, using marker-gene and graph evidence to review uncertain relationships.
Extended the agent with spatial trajectory proposal, relation adjudication, ordering review, and comparison with nonspatial trajectories by combining tissue adjacency and molecular evidence.

Implemented expression-weighted shortest-path pseudotime for spatially separate instances of a shared process, with synthetic negative controls and perturbation tests for spatial dependence and ordering stability.
Added JSON schema validation, corrective LLM retries, resumable execution, provenance logging, expert-supplied annotations, and preprocessed Seurat inputs including scATAC-seq gene-activity data.
Designed and implemented bPOS, an exact branch-aware metric that jointly evaluates lineage membership and within-lineage ordering using scalable block processing and inclusion-exclusion counting.

Diagnosed a bug in dyneval-based F1branches evaluation; reimplemented its published Jaccard, recovery, relevance, and harmonic-mean definition over the full cell scope and added diagnostic comparisons.
Built reproducible comparisons with Monocle 3, Slingshot, and TSCAN and curated gold-standard, silver-standard, and synthetic trajectory benchmarks.

projects.name: Med2State
projects.description: I am developing Med2State, a framework for learning structured patient-state representations from available multimodal clinical evidence and longitudinal history.
highlights: Designing configurable encoders and evidence fusion for demographics, vital signs, structured EHR events, text, and images, with explicit handling of available input sources.

Organizing each state representation into DX, PROC, and TREAT semantic channels for disease-related information, procedures, and treatment or medication exposure, using evidence available up to a defined time point.
Investigating learning from partial evidence and longitudinal context, with concept readouts and retrieval-based evaluation to test what information each channel retains.

The earlier prototype aligned BioClinicalBERT note embeddings with structured EHR events, fused them through multi-head cross-attention, and implemented a Med2Vec-compatible PyTorch model with component ablations.

projects.name: PaperEval
projects.description: I built data pipelines and LLM-based workflows for acceptance prediction, manuscript assessment, and review-response evaluation.
highlights: Built Selenium and asynchronous OpenReview pipelines with JSON storage and resumable checkpoints for papers, reviews, scores, author responses, and metadata; extracted author contact information from PDFs with PyMuPDF.

Fine-tuned GPT-4o for acceptance prediction with progressively richer inputs: paper metadata, reviewer scores, and review comments. Implemented training-data preparation and classification evaluation.
Developed agent workflows for manuscript and figure assessment, review-response scoring, and response generation; evaluated generated responses against replies from accepted and rejected submissions.
Designed a bounded Gaussian-noise mapping from acceptance levels to continuous constructiveness targets.

projects.name: Overlapping Group LASSO
projects.description: I compared overlapping group LASSO implementations and implemented an optimized algorithm in C for integration with R.
highlights: Compared overlapping_LeastR from the MATLAB SLEP library with oglasso in VennLasso under matched problem sizes and convergence tolerances.
Simulated 1,000 large sparse-matrix datasets with overlapping groups and compared runtime using t-tests.

projects.name: Data-Intensive Research
projects.description: I implemented research data-collection infrastructure and synthesized literature on the effects of generative AI.
highlights: Built a LinkedIn crawler for 7,063 profiles using DrissionPage, depth-first search, multithreading, persistent SQLite storage, and resumable checkpoints.
Implemented error logging and automated gap recovery for a Google Patents collection pipeline handling approximately 300 GB of Chinese patent text.
Screened 50 papers and organized 13 core studies into a focused literature review.

projects.name: MUDAC 2025
projects.description: I developed features and models for sparse, high-dimensional numerical and text data in the Midwest Undergraduate Data Analysis Competition.
highlights: Encoded data using embeddings, sentiment scores, and pairwise similarities.
Applied Cox proportional hazards regression and a causal Bayesian network to study match duration and closure.
Designed a mixture-of-experts model with regression, MLP, and Transformer experts and a learned gating network; compared with random forest and XGBoost.

projects.name: Public Health Equity Data Challenge
projects.description: I analyzed questionnaire data on inequities in access to mental-health resources and co-authored the analysis report and poster.
highlights: Applied multiple regression, ridge regression, decision trees, and causal inference methods.
Built a mental-health prediction interface in tkinter backed by an AdaBoost model in scikit-learn.

projects.name: Financial Forecasting Thesis
projects.description: My undergraduate thesis compared statistical and neural forecasting models for stock-market and cryptocurrency time series.
highlights: Collected and harmonized data from Wind and Yahoo Finance; implemented ARIMA in R and LSTM and Transformer models in PyTorch.
Adapted Transformer input embeddings and feature weighting and compared models across the Shanghai Composite, Nasdaq, and CMC200 indices.

projects.name: Carbon Emission Rights Pricing
projects.description: I studied carbon-emission trading prices using macroeconomic, fossil-fuel price, and policy variables constructed from Wind data.
highlights: Diagnosed underfitting in R regression models and examined associations between carbon prices and policy variables.
Implemented vector autoregression and impulse-response analysis in R and LSTM forecasting in TensorFlow.
